Motto: Tomorrow Needs Michigan Tech
Michigan Technological University (Michigan Tech, MTU, or simply Tech) is a public research university in Houghton, Michigan, United States.
The main Michigan Tech campus is located in Houghton, Michigan—north of US 41 and south of the Portage Canal.

Michigan Tech was founded in 1885 as the Michigan Mining School.[7] After much agitation by Jay Abel Hubbell, the state legislature established the school to train mining engineers. Hubbell donated land for the school's first buildings.[8]
The school started with four faculty members and twenty-three students. It was housed in the Houghton Fire Hall from 1886 through 1889.[9]
Former names: Michigan Mining School (1885–1897)Michigan College of Mines (1897–1927)Michigan College of Mining and Technology (1927–1964)
In 1964, one of the final years of his presidency, the school changed from a college to a university, changing its name a final time to Michigan Technological University.

The university comprises five colleges and schools: the College of Engineering, the College of Computing, the College of Sciences and Arts, the College of Business, and the College of Forest Resources and Environmental Science.
The undergraduate degree programs, together with masters and doctoral degrees are offered across the college's nine departments:

Michigan Tech offers more than 120 undergraduate and graduate degrees in engineering, natural and physical sciences, computing, business and economics, technology, environmental studies, arts, humanities, and social sciences.
The university has historically been focused on engineering, and as of November 2022, 57% of students are enrolled in the College of Engineering.
As of the fall semester in 2021, the total enrollment at Michigan Technological University is 6,977.
As of 2025, Michigan Tech has 495 faculty.[84]
The university is governed by an eight-member board of trustees whose members are appointed by the governor of Michigan and confirmed by the Michigan Senate.[62][63]

value.text:
Michigan Technological University, commonly known as Michigan Tech or MTU, is a public research university in Houghton, Michigan, United States. Its main campus lies between US 41 and the Portage Canal. The institution was founded in 1885 as the Michigan Mining School, established by the state legislature to train mining engineers. It began with four faculty members and twenty-three students, and occupied the Houghton Fire Hall from 1886 through 1889. The school became the Michigan College of Mines in 1897 and the Michigan College of Mining and Technology in 1927. In 1964 it became a university and adopted its present name.

The university is organized into five colleges covering engineering, computing, sciences and arts, business, and forest resources and environmental science. Its academic offerings extend from undergraduate study to master’s and doctoral degrees, spanning engineering, natural and physical sciences, technology, environmental studies, humanities and social sciences. Its engineering heritage remains prominent: in November 2022, 57 percent of students were enrolled in the College of Engineering. Total enrollment was 6,977 in the fall semester of 2021. In 2025 the university reported 495 faculty members. It is governed by an eight-member board of trustees appointed by Michigan’s governor and confirmed by the Michigan Senate.

Its engineering heritage remains prominent: in November 2022, 57 percent of students were enrolled in the College of Engineering. Total enrollment was 6,977 in the fall semester of 2021. In 2025 the university reported 495 faculty members. It is governed by an eight-member board of trustees appointed by Michigan’s governor and confirmed by the Michigan Senate.
